4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the Planning Commission. All Oral Communications speaker requests must be received by the Clerk by the start of oral
communications. Up to 30 minutes are available for comments on items not on the agenda. Remarks must be addressed to the Planning Commission as a whole. State law prohibits Planning Commission action on non-agenda items. As appropriate, comments may be referred to the City Manager for follow-up or placement on a future agenda. Please be aware that the Mayor has the authority to reduce equally each speaker’s time to accommodate a larger number of speakers.
5.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act (open meetings for local bodies, California Government Code Section 54950 et seq.).
6.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a speaker request to the City Clerk. Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the Planning Commission. Please be aware that the Chair has the authority to reduce equally each speaker’s time to accommodate a larger number of speakers. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Planning Commissioner or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
6A.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES of the August 6, 2026, Planning Commission meeting.
STAFF CONTACT: Deana Gay, Planning Commission Clerk
Staff recommends approval.
Minutes of August 6, 2026
6B.
PROJECT NAME: Cordato Duplex Addition and Remodel; CASE NUMBERS: MULTI-007416-2024, DR-007483-2024, and CDPNF-007484-2024; FILING DATE: July 22, 2024; APPLICANT: Cordato Family Trust; LOCATION: 1490 & 1492 Summit Avenue (APN: 260-630-35-00); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: A design review permit and coastal development permit to allow a first and second floor addition and remodel to an existing two-story duplex; ZONING/OVERLAY: Residential 11 (R-11) and Coastal Overlay Zone; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: The project has been determined to be exempt from environmental review pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) which exempts additions to existing structures provided that the addition will not result in an increase of more than 50 percent of the floor area of the structures before the addition, or 2,500 square feet, whichever is less. The proposed addition totals 1,047 square feet which is less than 50 percent of the floor area of the structures before the addition and less than the allowable 2,500-square foot threshold under this exemption. None of the exceptions in Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines apply and no historical resources will be impacted by the proposed development.
STAFF CONTACT: Kaipo Eager-Kaninau, Associate Planner, (760) 633-2717 or kkaninau@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends approval.
Cordato Duplex Addition and Remodel - Report
6C.
PROJECT NAME: Forestdale Slope Repair; CASE NUMBER: MULTI-007802-2025; DR-007803-2025; CDPNF-007804-2025; FILING DATE: 01/09/2025; APPLICANT: Village Park Townhome Corporation #3; High Country Villas Management Corporation; LOCATION: 1882 Forestdale Drive (APNs: 259-222-17-00; 259-222-47-00); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Design review and coastal development permit for the construction of a soil nail wall to repair a manufactured slope and associated private drainage facilities within natural slopes; ZONING/OVERLAY: R-8/Coastal Overlay/Special Study Overlay; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, Section 15304(c) – Class 4 –
(minor alterations to land) which exempts minor public or private alterations in the condition of land, water, and/or vegetation which do not involve removal of healthy, mature, scenic trees. The project is consistent with this exemption, as it proposes the repair of a slope and associate drainage facilities with minimal land disturbance. While there is Southern Maritime Chaparral onsite, which is a sensitive biological resource, the project will avoid removal of sensitive vegetation, therefore, none of the exceptions prescribed under Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines apply and no historic resources are affected by the proposed project
STAFF CONTACT: Fran Carr, Senior Planner, (760) 633-2738 or fcarr@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends approval.
Forest Dale Slope Repair - Report
6D.
PROJECT NAME: Pastaria Vivi Alcohol License; CASE NUMBER: MULTI-008417-2025, USE-008538-2025, DR-008537-2025; FILING DATE: November 24, 2025; APPLICANT: Brandon Jennings, Pastaria Vivi, LLC; LOCATION: 119 N El Camino Real, Unit: G (APN: 259-121-24); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Minor Use Permit (MIN) and Design Review Permit (DR) to authorize a new type 41 alcohol license for an existing restaurant and exterior improvements including an outdoor patio dining area; ZONING/OVERLAY: General Commercial (GC) Zone within the El Camino Real Specific Plan; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: The project has been determined to be exempt from environmental review pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) which exempts the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, licensing of private structures which would include the licensing for alcohol service for a proposed restaurant. The project meets this criterion. None of the exceptions in Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines apply, and no historical resources will be impacted by the proposed development.
STAFF CONTACT: Hoger Saleh, Assistant Planner: (760) 633-2714 or hsaleh@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends approval.
Pastaria Vivi Alcohol License - Report

8A.
PROJECT NAME: Camino Condos; CASE NUMBER: MULTI-008443-2025; DR-008454-2025; SUB-008455-2025 FILING DATE: October 21, 2025; APPLICANT: Brian Grover, Nolen Communities; LOCATION: East of El Camino Real, north of Garden View Road (257-470-24-00); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Design review permit and tentative map to construct an 87-unit condominium building on a vacant 1.93 acre site in the New Encinitas community; ZONING/OVERLAY: General Commercial Zone, Residential 30 Overlay; Scenic/Visual Corridor, Hillside/Inland Bluff, Cultural/Natural Resources Overlay; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: The project has been determined to be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Public Resources Code Section 21080.66 which exempts qualified urban infill housing development projects if: it is located in an urban area; is on an “urban infill site”; is less than 20 acres; is not in an environmentally sensitive area; is consistent with the local
general plan and zoning; achieves at least one-half the default density; does not involve demolition of a historic structure; and does not include a transient lodging use. The proposed project is a qualified housing development project, therefore is exempt from CEQA.
STAFF CONTACT: Denise Russell, Principal Planner, (760) 633-2716 or drussell@encinitasca.gov.

8B.
CASE NUMBER: PLCY-008977-2026 GPA/LCPA; APPLICANT: City of Encinitas; LOCATION: Citywide; PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Public hearing to consider a recommendation to the City Council for the adoption of the Resource Management Element (RME) update. The City is conducting a focused amendment to the RME of its General Plan to address equitable access to open space, rewilding, climate resilience, and habitat connectivity pursuant to Senate Bill 1425 and Assembly Bill 1889. The draft RME amendment is available on the City’s website at: encinitasca.gov/resourcemanagement. A General Plan Amendment (GPA) and Local Coastal Program Amendment (LCPA) are proposed to reflect the adoption of the RME update. ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: Pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, the project is exempt pursuant to Section 15307 (Class 7), Section 15308 (Class 8), and Section 15300.2. Section 15307 provides a categorical exemption for actions taken by regulatory agencies, as authorized by State law or local ordinance, to assure the maintenance, restoration, or enhancement of a natural resource where the regulatory process involves procedures for protection of the environment. Section 15308 provides a categorical exemption for actions taken by regulatory agencies, as authorized by State or local ordinance, to assure the maintenance, restoration, enhancement, or protection of the environment where the regulatory process involves procedures for protection of the environment. Section 15300.2 identifies a series of exceptions, that if applicable, prohibit the application of a categorical exemption and therefore preclude a project from being found categorically exempt. The proposed project is not identified as a prohibited exception; and therefore, the exemption applies.
STAFF CONTACT: Evan Jedynak, Senior Planner – Mobility Coordinator: (760) 633-2686 or ejedynak@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends the Planning Commission make a recommendation to the City Council
